description:
I want to inspire people who have always dreamed about building a treehouse to give themselves permission to make it real. These structures have a way of connecting us to nature, to each other, and to something lasting and magical.  Too often, the permitting process or the fear of how to start stops people before they even begin. My message is simple: you can do this. You do not have to build alone. There is a whole community ready to help you along the way. It is about creativity, collaboration, and bringing a little more wonder into the world, one treehouse at a time. Pete Nelson transformed a childhood dream—a simple tree fort built with his father in New Jersey—into a movement that reconnects people with the natural world through pioneering sustainable architecture and elevated living.
As founder of Nelson Treehouse, Pete has redefined what's possible when imagination meets craftsmanship among the branches. His innovative designs have elevated treehouses from childhood playgrounds
title: Treehouses NOW | Pete Nelson | TEDxFargo

This talk challenges us to rethink what caregiving really means and how we can create healthier, more human ways to care for the people we love while navigating our own lives. As a systems engineer, business development manager, and digital strategist across three continents, Isabel kept encountering the same puzzle: Why do brilliant people feel inexplicably stuck? After navigating her own journey as an expat mother managing competing priorities across countries and cultures, she discovered the answer: We're anchored by stories about our past that we’ve mistaken for truth.
Now an EMCC Senior Practitioner and founder of Motiva Coaching & Supervision, Isabel specialises in helping driven professionals courageously face their personal history and rewrite it as aprendizajes—transformative wisdom that opens the path to fulfilling relationships and prosperity. title: Defining balance for the sandwich generation | Isabel Vallejo Echavarría | TEDxThonglor Women

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if the biggest problem with education isn't AI—but the system that existed long before AI arrived?

In this thought-provoking TEDx talk, Sanjay Divakar draws on his experience attending schools across India, Dubai, and the United States to question whether traditional education is preparing students for the world they will actually inherit.

From memorization and following instructions to rigid schedules and standardized measures of success, Sanjay explores how schools have been designed around predictability—even though the future increasingly demands adaptability, creativity, and the ability to ask better questions.

He argues that AI isn't breaking education. It's revealing where education was already broken.

If machines can memorize, calculate, generate, and complete tasks faster than humans, then perhaps the question isn't how we can compete with AI. It's whether we should continue measuring human potential by the same standards in the first place.

title: Education Was Built for a World That No Longer Exists | Sanjay Divakar | TEDxThird Ward Salon

author: TEDx Talks
description: In this TEDx talk, Baba Cedrick invites us to see the djembe not just as an instrument, but as a living model for community. By breaking down its parts, (i.e. the shell, the skin, the rings, and the rope) he reveals a powerful insight he learned from the djembe: strong communities are built through intentional roles, shared tension, and connection. Blending storytelling, cultural wisdom, and live drumming, he challenges us to rethink leadership, honor emerging voices, and understand tension not as a threat, but as the source of harmony. Baba Cedrick (Abiono) Ogunrinde is a master West African drummer, educator, and culture bearer whose work explores rhythm as a pathway to connection, healing, and community. A Djembefola with over three decades of study, he trained under renowned masters including Famadou Konaté, Mamady Keita, and the late Bernard Woma. His musical lineage spans Guinea, Mali, Ghana, and Nigeria, and his artistry has appeared on global stages, from professional dance co
title: What a West African Drum Can Teach About Community | Baba Cedrick Ogunrinde | TEDxThird Ward Salon

author: TEDx Talks
description: What can rural communities teach us about strength, leadership, and care? Drawing on his experiences living across Western Canada, David Chang explores the lessons embedded within rural communities and the important perspectives they offer in an increasingly changing world. His talk invites us to reconsider the value of community, connection, and the places that shape us. David Chang is a second-year medical student at the University of British Columbia. He grew up across Western Canada, spending time in Alberta, the Interior, Vancouver Island, and now the Lower Mainland. He completed his undergraduate studies in Biology at the University of Victoria and has interests in rural medicine, health advocacy, and substance use treatment. Outside of medicine, David enjoys volleyball, rock climbing, and playing the drums. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Voices Unheard: What Rural Communities Teach us | David Chang | TEDxUBC

description:
Have you ever made a decision and felt completely certain that you chose it? What if your brain had already begun making that decision before you were even aware of it?

In his talk, Kia Bahari explores the intersection of neuroscience and philosophy to examine one of humanity’s oldest questions: do we really have free will? By looking at what brain science can tell us about how decisions are made, he invites us to reconsider our assumptions about choice, responsibility, and what it means to be human. Kia Bahari is a medical student at UBC, educator, and content creator with a passion for making complex ideas accessible. He is the founder of his own tutoring company and educational YouTube platform, where he helps students navigate challenging university coursework and prepare for the MCAT. His interests span medicine, neuroscience, education, and the questions that emerge at the intersection of science and philosophy. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference forma
title: Inside the Moment You Think, You Decide: Exploring Free Will | Kia Bahari | TEDxUBC

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if losing a match could be just as valuable as winning one?
For many young athletes, sports can feel like they are all about the scoreboard, medals, trophies, and being the best. But sport teaches us something much bigger than how to win. It teaches us how to grow.
In this talk, 12-year-old Sasath explores the idea that winning is not the only measure of success. Every training session, every mistake, every defeat, and every challenge is an opportunity to become stronger, more disciplined, and more confident.
Through the world of sports, Sasath shares how losing can teach resilience, competition can teach respect, practice can build discipline, and setbacks can help us discover what we are capable of achieving.
The final score tells us who won the game—but it does not tell the whole story.
The real victory is in becoming a better version of yourself than you were yesterday. V. P. Sasath Pasandul Vitharana is a 12-year-old student of Trinity College, Kandy, with a passion for spor
title: Winning Isn’t Everything — Growing Is | Sasath Pasandul Vitharana | TEDxKandy

description: Before we ever learn to speak, we learn to listen. Music has always been one of humanity's oldest and most universal forms of expression, capable of communicating emotions that words often fail to capture. In this talk, Chahir explores how music transcends language, culture, and background, becoming a shared human experience that connects us all. More than just an art form, music is an invitation to create, to belong, and to express who we are.  Chahir Mansour is a professional drummer and the band manager of Stage 5. A recent Finance & Investment graduate from the Georgia State University, Cairo University joint program, Chahir has balanced his academic journey with a deep passion for music. Having managed and performed in more than 14 concerts across Egypt, he brings firsthand insight into the country's growing music scene and believes in the power of music to connect people beyond words. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized
title: A Language Words Can't Speak | Chahir Mansour | TEDxCairo University

author: TEDx Talks
description: Stress has become one of the defining emotions of modern life. We spend so much time trying to avoid it, suppress it, or escape it, but what if we've been asking the wrong question all along? In this talk, Dr. Mohamed challenges the way we think about stress by exploring why it exists in the first place. Blending psychology, neuroscience, and biology, he unpacks how stress shapes not only our thoughts and decisions, but also the way our bodies function, from the brain to the body's physiological responses. Dr. Mohamed ElShorbagy is a medical doctor, science communicator, and content creator dedicated to making science accessible to everyone. Believing that knowledge should challenge misconceptions rather than reinforce them, he founded ما وراء النضارة, a platform that simplifies complex scientific concepts and debunks common myths. His work has gained regional and international recognition, including being a FameLab finalist by the British Council and winning the Best Climate Content
title: Forest Tiger VS Email:Which is worse for your brain? | Dr. Mohamed ElShorbagy | TEDxCairo University

description: Can too much of a good thing become harmful? And can what we fear the most eventually become our greatest strength? Drawing on Carl Jung's concept of Enantiodromia; the idea that everything, when pushed to its extreme, transforms into its opposite, Doha explores the delicate balance that shapes both individuals and civilizations. Through a fascinating blend of geology, Egyptology, ancient history, philosophy, and personal reflection, her talk reveals how nature, history, and even our own lives are governed by the same timeless pattern: every extreme carries the seed of its opposite. Doha Abdallah is a licensed tour guide and a graduate of the Faculty of Tourism Guidance, where she graduated top of her class with academic excellence. Passionate about Egyptology, she is known for bringing Ancient Egypt to life through its everyday stories, correcting common misconceptions, and uncovering lesser-known insights that deepen our understanding of one of history's greatest civilizations. title: The Battle of Opposites | Doha Abdallah | TEDxCairo University

description: What if your greatest obstacle isn't failure, but your own potential? We're often taught that being "full of potential" is something to be proud of. But what happens when potential becomes a place we hide? In this talk, Norhan explores the subtle trap of endless preparation, self-improvement, and waiting for the "right time." Through personal experiences and hard-earned lessons, she challenges the audience to stop treating potential as an identity and start turning it into action. Because the greatest loss isn't failing, it's never discovering what you're truly capable of. Norhan Nada is a Computer Engineering student at Cairo University, a technology enthusiast, and a public speaker passionate about innovation and personal growth. Her journey has taken her from winning Red Bull Basement Egypt to reaching the global Top 10 in Tokyo, claiming first place at the GEM Hackathon, and representing Egypt at international conferences in Serbia and Turkey. title: Proof Over Potential | Norhan Nada | TEDxCairo University

description: Sondos explores the hidden role of insecurity in shaping the way we perceive others. Through personal experiences and everyday interactions, she uncovers how comparison, judgment, and even envy often say far more about ourselves than the people standing in front of us. By learning to understand the emotions beneath our reactions, we can build healthier relationships, not just with others, but with ourselves. Because genuine human connection begins with honest self-awareness. Sondos Amr is a second-year medical student at Ain Shams University with a deep interest in psychology, human behavior, and the emotions that shape our everyday interactions. Passionate about understanding the connection between self-awareness and meaningful relationships, she explores how the conversations we have with ourselves influence the way we connect with the world around us. Through her talk, Sondos invites audiences to look inward, not with judgment, but with curiosity. This talk was given at a TEDx even
title: It All Starts From Within | Sondos Amr | TEDxCairo University

description: Why do we travel thousands of miles to discover places, but rarely explore the one we already call home? In this talk, Marwan challenges the way we experience the places we call home. Through architecture, history, food, and everyday encounters, he reveals that every street, neighborhood, and hidden corner holds stories waiting to be discovered. By learning to see our surroundings through the eyes of a traveler, we don't just uncover new places; we build a deeper connection with our culture, our communities, and the places that have been shaping us all along.  Marwan R. Ojaimie is a Lebanese architect, storyteller, content creator, and the founder of Visit Amioun. Through his work across Lebanon and Egypt, he documents places, people, heritage, and everyday stories, inspiring hundreds of thousands of people to see their surroundings through a different lens. title: Why Does Everything Look Better Somewhere Else? | Marwan Ojaimie | TEDxCairo University

Todos comemos, es uno de los actos más cotidianos de nuestra vida, pero pocas veces nos detenemos a pensar en todo lo que hay detrás de cada alimento.

La gastronomía puede ser mucho más que preparar y disfrutar un plato: puede convertirse en una herramienta para crear negocios con propósito, impulsar la economía circular, generar impacto social y cuidar el ambiente.

A partir de la historia de la palta, el “oro verde”, esta charla propone mirar la gastronomía desde una nueva perspectiva: como una oportunidad para transformar nuestra manera de producir, consumir y relacionarnos con el planeta.

Rocío Giménez nos invita a descubrir cómo la gastronomía puede convertirse en una herramienta de transformación, capaz de generar impacto económico, social y ambiental. Porque cada elección que hacemos alrededor de la mesa también puede ser una elección sobre el futuro que queremos construir. Directora de la primera Academia de Gastronomía de Triple impacto. title: Gastronomía de triple impacto: El Oro Verde | Rocío Gimenez | TEDxCosquín

description: Grief will never disappear - but it doesn’t have to isolate us. By opening the conversation, we make space for healing, connection, and community. Grief shared is grief lightened. Charlotte is a junior from Richmond, Virginia, majoring in psychology with minors in leadership studies and childhood studies. She is part of the Masters in Teaching program where she is studying elementary education, following her dream of being a kindergarten teacher. She's on the executive board for CNU's Special Olympics Gymnastics organization, and can best be found spending time in schools, with the children she babysits, or at a Mexican restaurant.
